subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — availability thresholds & scheduled upgrades
messages:
From: Maya Singh <contracts@brightlane.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hsu <legal@brightlane.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA v2 redlines — SLA/maintenance clarifications

Soojin,

Thanks for sending the MSA and Order Form draft. Our legal team has a few focused redlines on the SLA and support terms before we can proceed to signature. Major items below — attaching a marked-up Word for reference (BL_MSA_v2_redlines.docx).

1) Availability target: We would like to see 99.95% for the hosted endpoints used by BrightLane (production API). Current draft lists 99.9% which is material for our customers.

2) Service credits: Please confirm the calculation method and add a hard cap (we propose max credit = 50% of monthly fees for the impacted service) and that credits are applied to the next billing cycle. Also ask that credits are automatic after an incident is validated.

3) Scheduled maintenance / upgrade windows: We need to limit weekly scheduled maintenance to a single 6-hour window per week for non-critical upgrades and require minimum 14 days advance notice for any rolling upgrade that affects production availability. Emergency maintenance (security patches) can be excluded but should be communicated within 24 hours.

4) Response times / P1 definition: Tighten the P1 response/resolution ladder and add an explicit 2-hour response SLA for P1 incidents.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these points or propose compromise language? We have a hard target to finalize the contract by EOD Sep 30 to keep the Q4 deployment on track.

Best,
Maya Singh
Head of Legal Operations — BrightLane

Attachments: BL_MSA_v2_redlines.docx
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <contracts@brightlane.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <legal@brightlane.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA v2 redlines — SLA/maintenance clarifications

Maya — thanks for the clear summary and the marked-up doc. Looping in our legal and ops leads (below) to get aligned quickly. High-level positions from Redwood for negotiation:

- Availability: We can offer a higher availability tier (99.95%) but it needs to be tied to the Dedicated capacity SKU or a specified minimum monthly committed capacity. For our standard hosted tier we typically commit 99.9%. Can you confirm which SKU BrightLane will use?

- Credits: Agree to automatic credits once incident is validated, and we can accept a cap at 50% of the monthly service fees for the affected service. We'll propose explicit calculation language (see attached uptime-matrix.xlsx) that maps minutes of downtime to credit percentage.

- Maintenance windows: Ops preference is a 4-hour weekly maintenance window with 7 days notice for non-breaking changes. For customers requiring 14 days notice and stricter windows we recommend Dedicated with contractual SLAs and a Maintenance Addendum. We can, however, accept a 14-day notice clause for rolling upgrades that modify API behavior. Emergency security patches will be excluded but Redwood will provide incident reports within 24 hours of remediation.

- P1 response: We can commit to a 2-hour initial response for P1s and a best-effort resolution timeline; resolution SLA remains dependent on root cause. We will include an escalation ladder and a 48-hour initial mitigation commitment.

Next steps: Lauren — can you review the proposed redline language (I attached a first-pass doc) and advise if we should accept the 14-day notice or push for Dedicated as the contractual requirement? Kimberly — ops, confirm whether the 4-hour weekly window is operationally feasible and whether there is any anticipated uplift to deployment cadence if we accept 14-day pre-notice.

Maya / Tom — I'll follow up with a tracked redline and Docusign flow by Monday. If we can close by Sep 30 that's ideal; otherwise we'll need to flag dates for the Q4 deployment.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0191

Attachments: uptime-matrix.xlsx; BL_MSA_v2_redlines.docx (for reference)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: BrightLane — proposed SLA redline language (draft)

Team — thread copy below. I drafted proposed redline text to give legal something concrete. Please reply inline with edits; we need to send an external counter by Monday morning. Key bullets: uptime tiers, definition of "Unavailable", maintenance definitions, credits calc, and P1 ladder.

Proposed snippets (to be inserted into SLA section):

1) Definitions:
"Unavailable" — A Redwood-hosted endpoint will be considered "Unavailable" when 1) requests return 5xx errors for the API surface used by the customer, or 2) average end-to-end p95 latency for the configured API route exceeds 10x the baseline measured over the prior 30-day period, and such condition persists for at least 5 consecutive minutes. Loss of new session creation due to authentication backend issues will also be considered Unavailable if affecting >10% of requests.

"Scheduled Maintenance" — Routine updates that may temporarily affect performance but are pre-announced and performed within an agreed maintenance window. "Scheduled Maintenance" does not include Emergency Maintenance.

2) Availability tiers / credits table (summary):
- Hosted Standard: 99.9% uptime — credits start at 99.5% and escalate per the attached uptime-matrix.
- Dedicated / Committed: 99.95% uptime — available if customer signs up to the Dedicated capacity SKU or a minimum monthly commit of $X (TBD).

3) Maintenance / notice:
- By default Redwood will schedule non-breaking maintenance in a single weekly 4-hour window. Customer will receive at least 7 days' notice for routine maintenance.
- For Rolling Upgrades that may change API behavior or require client updates, Redwood will provide at least 14 days' advance notice and a rollback procedure.
- Emergency Maintenance (e.g., zero-day security patches) may be performed outside the weekly window and will be communicated within 24 hours of action.

4) Credits / cap / cure period:
- Credits are applied to the next billing cycle once Redwood validates an incident and calculates downtime per the uptime matrix.
- Credit cap: 50% of the monthly fees attributable to the impacted service.
- Cure period: Customer must provide Redwood 48 hours after incident validation to accept remediation before credit is applied automatically (internal ops step: what does this mean for automated credits?).

5) P1 / response:
- Initial response time: 2 hours for P1 incidents (acknowledge and begin mitigation).
- Mitigation commitment: Redwood will aim for an initial material mitigation within 48 hours; root-cause and full resolution timelines are incident-dependent.

Please comment. Lauren — any wording you want tightened? Kimberly — can you confirm the 4-hour weekly window and whether we can accept the 14-day rolling-upgrade notice as a special-case? Aditya — ops cost impact for commiting a dedicated SKU vs hosted?

-- Soojin

----- Inline replies -----

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0700
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

I like the definitions; will tighten the Unavailable clause to avoid ambiguous latency multipliers — suggest replacing the 10x baseline wording with "p95 latency exceeds 2x the 30-day baseline for 10 consecutive minutes". Also remove the 48-hour cure requirement; legal prefers automatic credit triggers once incident is validated to avoid disputes. I will send tracked edits.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Ops: 4-hour weekly window is fine for most maintenance. 14-day notice for rolling upgrades is feasible but will require coordination with our release calendar; we should flag that behavior-altering upgrades need canary windows and optional opt-out for Dedicated customers.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 10:18:00 -0700
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Finance note: If BrightLane wants 99.95 on hosted without committing spend, we need to price that as an elevated SLA with reserve capacity. I'll draft a pricing blurb for inclusion in the Order Form.
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <contracts@brightlane.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <legal@brightlane.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA v2 redlines — availability thresholds & scheduled upgrades (final positions)

Maya / Tom — thanks again for the redlines and for the quick turnaround. Per our internal review above, please find Redwood's final positions and next steps below. I've attached the tracked changes file and the uptime matrix for transparency.

1) Availability: BrightLane may elect Either: (A) Dedicated / Committed capacity SKU (recommended) with a contractual availability of 99.95%, or (B) Hosted Standard with availability of 99.9%. If BrightLane signs the Dedicated SKU or commits to the minimum monthly spend identified in the Order Form, Redwood will include 99.95% in the MSA.

2) Credits: Redwood agrees to automatic credits once an incident is validated by our incident team. Credits will be calculated per the attached uptime-matrix and applied to the next billing cycle. Credit cap will be 50% of the monthly fees for the impacted service. Per Lauren's feedback, we will remove the 48-hour cure requirement and surface the incident validation process in the SLA notes to reduce ambiguity.

3) Maintenance and rolling upgrades:
- Default routine maintenance: one weekly 4-hour window; Redwood will provide 7 days' notice for routine maintenance.
- Rolling upgrades that may change API behavior: Redwood will provide 14 days' advance notice and publish an upgrade plan and rollback procedure. Customers on Dedicated can opt for narrower windows or blackout periods via the Order Form addendum.
- Emergency Maintenance: can occur outside the weekly window; Redwood will notify the customer within 24 hours and provide a post-incident report.

4) P1 response: Redwood will commit to a 2-hour initial response for P1 incidents and will publish an escalation ladder. Resolution timelines remain incident-specific; Redwood will provide mitigation updates every 6 hours for active P1s until the issue is contained.

Next steps:
- Attached: BL_MSA_v2_redlines.docx (tracked), uptime-matrix.xlsx
- I've prepared a countersigned Order Form draft and opened a DocuSign envelope for the Order Form: https://app.docusign.com/BL-MSA-2026
- Request: Please review our tracked redlines and countersign the Order Form by EOD Sep 30 if possible. If you require further negotiation on the Dedicated pricing line, we should schedule a 30-minute call this week (I copied Aditya for pricing).

If we don't receive a signature by Sep 30 we'll continue to support BrightLane on a standard hosted plan (99.9% SLA) while procurement finalizes the Dedicated addendum.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call to walk through any specific redline language.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0191

summary: External asked to clarify maintenance windows and service credit calculation; internal legal and ops proposed specific redline language and positions; final reply confirms options for 99.95 via Dedicated or 99.9 hosted, accepts 50% credit cap and automatic credits, and requests signature by Sep 30.
